lead.overview: See how your account is doing at a glance and get to its settings.
lead.fleet: Your vehicle inventory, how much each one is used, what they cost and the group tree.
lead.maintenance: What needs attention, work orders, service plans and the catalogs of workshops and parts.
lead.routes: Today's dispatch, planned routes and the places your vehicles visit.
lead.reports: The indicator dashboard, reports and the ones sent on a schedule.
lead.integrations: The API, webhooks, automations, sensors and data exchange in files.
lead.users: Who gets into the account, with which role and which vehicles they see.
lead.roles: The account's roles and what each one allows.
lead.vehicleGroups: Group your vehicles by branch, route or whatever works for you, and filter the list and the map by group.
lead.activity: Who did what and when in this account.
lead.profile: Your details, how you see the platform and your privacy.
lead.accounts: Every account on the platform, with its status, quotas and modules.
lead.settings: Sign-up, quotas for new accounts, map, addresses and passwords.
lead.signIn: Which other services people can sign in and create their account with, besides their email and password.
lead.storage: The external storage where backups are also kept.
lead.backups: When backups are made, which ones exist and how to download or restore them.
lead.simulator: Simulated GPS devices that connect like a real one, to test the platform without hardware.
lead.logs: The platform's numbers right now and what its administration did.
lead.notifications: Who is told about each alert, and through which channel.
lead.channels: The channels the platform notifies through. They are connected once, here, and every account uses them.
lead.systemNotifications: Who the platform tells about what happens to it: backups, disk, channels and new accounts.
lead.updates: Current version, latest available and what's new.

stats.eventsNote: alerts and notices of the last day

platform.title: Platform
platform.lead: The numbers of the whole installation

photo.failed: We couldn't save the photo. Try again.
photo.unreadable: We couldn't open that image. Try a JPG, PNG or WebP photo.

profile.appearanceLead: Light or dark mode is saved with your user and follows you to other devices.
profile.languageLead: The language you see the platform in and get your emails and notifications in.
profile.deleteLead: Deletes your user and, if you are the owner, the account with all its data.
profile.leaveLead: You stop seeing this account's vehicles. Your own account stays intact.

contact.title: Phone
contact.lead: To get by SMS the notifications that include you.
contact.none: You don't have a phone yet.
contact.phoneNote: With its country code, for example +50499887766.

roles.note: Every role sees the vehicles in its scope. A custom role adds only the permissions you tick.
roles.name: Name

invite.title: Invite someone
invite.sent: Invitation sent to {{email}}. It expires in 7 days.

log.title: Delivery log
log.lead: The latest messages: where each one went and how it ended. What does not go out is retried several times, waiting longer each time.
log.empty: No message has been sent yet.

channelNote.webhook: To another system connected to the platform

headers.title: Headers
headers.note: Optional. Headers of your own that every delivery carries, such as the key the other system asks for (Authorization).
headers.name: Name of header {{n}}
headers.kept: Carries: {{names}}. Their values are not shown.

notify.unavailable: Needs to be connected in Notification channels

notifications.channelOff: This channel is off on the platform: the notification sends nothing until it is turned back on or you choose another.

list.title: Account notifications
list.note: Each notification says who is told, about what and through which channel. A person only receives what is about vehicles they can see.

empty.title: No notifications yet
empty.lead: Alerts show on the platform, but nobody receives a message outside it until you create a notification.

remove.title: Delete the notification
remove.body: The notification “{{name}}” stops sending messages. Its log is kept.

editor.name: Name
editor.scopeNote: Each person receives only what is about vehicles they can see.

personNote.sms: It reaches whoever has their phone in their profile, and only about vehicles they can see.
personNote.push: It reaches whoever has the platform's mobile app and is signed in on it, and only about vehicles they can see. The app is not available yet: the notification is ready for when they install it.
personNote.webhook: Each person chosen fills the variables of whoever receives it: they get a message of their own, and only about vehicles they can see.
personNote.webhookOnce: Custom does not use each person's details: a single message is sent per notification, if any of the people chosen can see the vehicle.

editor.addressesNote: One per line. They receive everything the notification covers, whoever reads them.
editor.noAddresses: Addresses written by hand are only changed by whoever sees the whole account.
editor.needEvents: Choose at least one alert type.

signIn.note: Each service turned on shows as a button on the sign-in page and on “Create your account”. Whoever has no account creates one by continuing with the service, accepting the terms shown next to the button; whoever already has an account signs in with the service if it confirms the email is theirs.
signIn.back: Return address: copy it into the service
signIn.enableNote: Off, its button does not show and nobody signs in with it.
signIn.secretNote: It is stored encrypted and never shown again. Leave it empty to keep the one already saved.
signIn.saved: Saved. It is in use now.

google.lead: Let people sign in and sign up with their Google account.
google.steps: At console.cloud.google.com, under “APIs & Services”, set up the consent screen and, under “Credentials”, create an “OAuth client ID” of type “Web application”. Paste the return address into “Authorized redirect URIs”.

github.lead: Let people sign in and sign up with their GitHub account.
github.steps: At github.com/settings/developers create an “OAuth App”. Paste the return address into “Authorization callback URL” and, once saved, generate a client secret.
github.clientIdNote: The one GitHub shows when the app is created.

facebook.lead: Let people sign in and sign up with their Facebook account.
facebook.steps: At developers.facebook.com create an app with “Facebook Login” and ask for the email permission. In its settings, paste the return address into “Valid OAuth Redirect URIs”. The details are under “App settings” → “Basic”.

apple.lead: Let people sign in and sign up with their Apple ID.
apple.steps: At developer.apple.com, under “Certificates, IDs & Profiles”, create a “Services ID” with “Sign in with Apple”, register your domain and paste the return address into “Return URLs”. Then create a “Key” with “Sign in with Apple” and download its .p8 file: it can only be downloaded once.
apple.clientIdNote: The identifier of the service, for example com.company.web.
apple.teamIdNote: The 10 characters of your team, top right on Apple's page.
apple.keyIdNote: The 10 characters of the key you created.

custom.title: Other
custom.lead: Any other service that speaks OpenID Connect: Microsoft, Keycloak, Auth0, Okta or your company's.
custom.steps: In the service, register a web application with the return address. It will give you a client ID, a secret and the address of its issuer.
custom.name: Button name
custom.issuerNote: The OpenID Connect “issuer”. The platform reads the rest from there.
custom.clientIdNote: The one the service gave you.
custom.scopesNote: Separated by spaces. openid and email are needed.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.note: Sign in without a password, with Face ID, a fingerprint, Windows Hello or a security key. Each person creates theirs in their profile.
passkeys.noHttps: This address does not allow them: passkeys need HTTPS and a domain.

channels.saved: Saved. It is already in use.

key.title: Access key
key.note: It is stored encrypted and is never shown again. Leave it empty to keep the one already there.
key.kept: Key saved · type to change it

cap.title: Monthly cap per account
cap.note: How many messages each account can send per month through this channel. Empty means no cap. What goes over the cap is not sent and stays in the account's log.

test.label: Send a test message to
test.sent: The test message went out to {{to}}.

email.lead: Sent through the platform's mail server: account confirmations, invitations, alerts and reports.

sms.fromNote: The Twilio number that sends, with its country code, or the identifier of a messaging service (it starts with MG).

webhook.lead: Calls another system, for example an SMS or WhatsApp gateway: you write the address, the headers and the body, with variables each notification fills.
webhook.addressNote: Variables go in the path or the parameters, not in the server. Their values are written the way a web address needs them.
webhook.bodyNote: Optional. If empty, every variable is sent as JSON. In JSON, each value comes ready to go between quotes; with a form Content-Type header, as in a web address.
webhook.variablesNote: Tap one to put it where the cursor was, in the address or the body. They also work in the value of the headers.
webhook.perPerson: The green ones are about whoever receives the notification: if you use any, one message is sent per person of the notification; otherwise, a single one for everyone.

variable.type: What happened, as data: speeding, sos, backup_failed, test
variable.title: The first line: Truck 1: speeding
variable.message: The title and the details in a single line, for an SMS or a chat
variable.time: When it happened, in ISO 8601 format
variable.name: The name of whoever receives the notification
variable.phone: Their phone, with its country code: +50499887766

channels.enableNote: When it is off, accounts cannot use it.

push.note: They reach whoever has the platform's mobile app and is signed in on it. The app is not available yet: notifications through this channel are ready and will start arriving once each person installs it.

list.title: System notifications
list.note: Each one is a destination and the things it wants to hear about. While there is none, problems reach the notifications email in the settings.

system.empty: There are no system notifications yet. Create one to hear about a backup that fails, a disk filling up or a channel that stops delivering.
system.logLead: The platform's latest messages: where each one went and how it ended.

event.disk_high: The server's disk is filling up
event.ingest_stalled: Positions from the GPS devices stopped arriving

editor.targetNote: An email or a phone: it fills the variables of whoever receives it in Custom.
editor.needEvents: Choose at least one thing to tell about.

settings.saved: Saved. It is already in use.

general.registrationOpenNote: Anyone can create an account. When it is off, only people who got an invitation by email can sign up.
general.quotasNote: How many vehicles and users each account created from now on can have. Empty means no limit. Existing accounts do not change.
general.modulesNote: The optional modules each account starts with. Afterwards they are changed account by account.
general.mapStyleNote: Address of the map style the web and the apps use.
general.geocoderNote: Turns coordinates into an approximate address. It starts with OpenStreetMap's free public service. Another service must be compatible with Nominatim and end in /reverse. Empty turns it off.
general.geocoderAgentNote: How the platform introduces itself when asking for addresses. OpenStreetMap's public service asks to say who it is and how to reach them. Empty goes back to the automatic one.
general.geocoderAgentAuto: Automatic: the platform's name and address
general.geocoderIntervalNote: Milliseconds between two requests to the service. OpenStreetMap's public one allows one per second: 1100.
general.routingNote: Traces the simulator's routes along streets. Out of the box it is OSRM's public service over OpenStreetMap data, free and with one query per second. Another service must speak OSRM's API. Empty turns it off.
general.claimWindowNote: Minutes a newly added GPS device has to send its first report. If it does not arrive, the identifier is freed.
general.maxPending: GPS waiting for their first report
general.maxPendingNote: How many newly added GPS, still without their first report, an account can have at once.
general.historyNote: Days of trips that are kept. Empty means no limit; with a limit, at least {{min}} days. Whatever is older is deleted and cannot be recovered.
general.traccarRetentionNote: Days the receiver keeps its own copies of positions already read. It does not affect the history.
general.maxUploadNote: In MB, for what users upload, such as the evidence of an incident. Up to {{max}}.
general.alertEmailNote: Receives the platform's problems while there is no notification in “System notifications”: a nearly full disk, a backup that fails. Once system notifications exist, they take over.
general.diskNote: Percentage of disk used from which a warning is sent.
general.alertEmailsPerHourNote: Maximum alert emails a single account can generate in an hour. It protects mailboxes from a badly tuned alert.
general.legalNote: Shown in the terms of use and the privacy policy.
general.reset: The settings above go back to their factory values: open sign-up, new accounts without quotas or modules, and the map, address service, time limits, notifications and legal details as they came. Passwords do not change.
general.shortenBody: You are going to keep only {{days}} days of trips. Older positions of every account are deleted and cannot be recovered.
general.defaultLanguageNote: For whoever has not chosen theirs yet, and for the emails and notifications that go to addresses written by hand and the platform's own.

passwords.title: Passwords
passwords.note: Applies to passwords created or changed from now on. Existing ones keep working.
passwords.rulesNote: This is how it is explained to whoever signs up: "{{hint}}"
passwords.reset: The password policy goes back to a minimum of 8 characters, with no other requirements.

mail.title: Mail server
mail.note: The platform's emails go out through here: account confirmation, password change, invitations, alerts and reports.
mail.customOn: The platform sends with the details below.
mail.customOff: When it is off, the platform sends no email.
mail.serverNote: Your email provider gives them. The usual choice is port 587 with STARTTLS.
mail.credentialsNote: The password is stored encrypted and is never shown again. Leave it empty to keep the one already there.
mail.passwordKept: Password saved · type to change it
mail.fromNote: Who appears as the author of the emails. The domain must be authorized with your provider.
mail.reset: Your own mail server stops being used and its details and saved password are deleted. The platform stops sending email.
mail.testSent: The mail server accepted the message to {{to}}. Check that mailbox.
mail.testNote: The test goes to your email, {{email}}, with what is saved.

mailTemplates.title: Email templates
mailTemplates.note: The emails the platform writes. You can change their words in each language; what you leave untouched goes out as it comes.
mailTemplates.subject: Subject
mailTemplates.heading: Heading
mailTemplates.bodyNote: Line breaks are kept in the email.
mailTemplates.actionNote: The button leads to the right link. The platform adds the address.
mailTemplates.variablesNote: Click one to put it where the cursor is. The platform fills it in when it sends.
mailTemplates.restoreNote: Goes back to the text the platform comes with, in {{language}}. It applies when you save.
mailTemplates.saved: Saved. The next emails go out like this.

verifyEmail.name: Email confirmation
verifyEmail.note: Sent when an account is created, with the link to confirm the email.

resetPassword.name: Password change
resetPassword.note: Sent when someone asks for a new password, with the link to create it.

existingAccount.name: Existing account
existingAccount.note: Sent to whoever tries to sign up with an email that already has an account.

invitation.name: Account invitation
invitation.note: Sent to whoever is invited to see an account's vehicles.

panic.name: Panic button
panic.note: Sent to the account's administrators when someone presses a vehicle's panic button.

panicUnattended.name: Unattended panic button
panicUnattended.note: Sent again when nobody attends to the panic button in time.

scheduledReport.name: Scheduled report
scheduledReport.note: Carries a scheduled report as an attachment, every day, week or month.

mailTest.name: Test email
mailTest.note: Sent with the “Send a test email” button to check the mail server.

storage.missing: Fill in the storage details first
storage.unreadableSecret: The saved secret key cannot be read on this server: it comes from another one, for example from a restored backup. Type it again and save.
storage.title: External storage
storage.note: A space outside the server, compatible with S3, where the platform keeps files. Backups use it today.
storage.enabledNote: When it is off, everything stays only on the server.
storage.providerNote: Who provides the service. If yours is not on the list, leave “Any other S3-compatible service”.
storage.secretNote: It is stored encrypted and is never shown again. Leave it empty to keep the one already there.
storage.bucketNote: It must already exist. The key needs permission to read, write and delete in it.
storage.regionNote: If your provider does not use regions, leave it empty: us-east-1 is used.
storage.endpointNote: The S3 service's address, with https; not its admin panel's. For example, https://s3.example.com.
storage.endpointNoteAws: With Amazon it can stay empty: it comes from the region.
storage.prefixNote: Inside the bucket, where the platform keeps its things. Empty is the root.
storage.flagsNote: Optional. Files are moved by rclone, and these are the arguments passed to it, one per line, as in other tools that use it. S3 ones, which start with --s3-, are accepted, plus some general ones, such as --header or --no-check-certificate.
storage.reset: External storage is turned off and its details, arguments and saved key are deleted. What is already stored there is not touched.
storage.testOk: The connection works with what is written: a test file was written, read and deleted.
storage.testOkUnsaved: The connection works with what is written: a test file was written, read and deleted. It still needs saving.

backups.signedOut: The platform went back to how it was in the backup and your session is no longer valid. <login>Sign in again</login> to see how it ended.
backups.unavailable: This server has no access to the databases to make backups. Check its connection variables.

banner.down: The platform is stopped while the server swaps the databases. This page catches up on its own in a few minutes.
banner.steps: First a backup of how everything is now is saved. Then, in less than a minute, the server stops the platform for a few minutes to swap the databases.
banner.done: Restore finished on {{at}}: the platform went back.
banner.doneTo: Restore finished on {{at}}: the platform went back to the backup of {{date}}.
banner.failed: The restore did not happen: {{reason}}. The platform keeps the data it had.
banner.failedTo: The restore to the backup of {{date}} did not happen: {{reason}}. The platform keeps the data it had.

schedule.title: Scheduled backups
schedule.note: Each backup includes the platform's database, the device receiver's database and the files users upload.
schedule.scheduledNote: When it is off, there are backups only when someone asks for one here.
schedule.frequencyNote: When scheduled backups run. Times are in UTC.
schedule.upcomingOff: With backups turned on, they would run, in your time: {{times}}.
schedule.cronHelp: Five fields: minute, hour, day of the month, month and day of the week (0 is Sunday). An asterisk means all, and <num>*/6</num> means every 6. For example, <num>30 3 * * 1</num> is every Monday at 03:30 UTC.
schedule.retentionNote: How long scheduled backups are kept before being deleted. Manual backups are never deleted automatically.
schedule.uploadNote: Besides staying on the server, each backup is uploaded to the bucket {{bucket}}. If the server is lost, the backup is still there.
schedule.uploadSetup: To keep backups outside the server, first set up the <storage>external storage</storage>.
schedule.reset: Backup scheduling goes back to the default: a daily backup at 00:00 UTC, kept for 7 days and not sent to external storage.

list.title: Backups
list.noteRestore: Each backup can be downloaded or restored: restoring takes the platform back to how it was at that moment.
list.noteDownload: From here you can download their files. This server has no access to the databases to restore them.
list.empty: There are no backups in the list yet.

discover.prompt: Are there backups in external storage that do not show here, such as another installation's? Look for them to be able to download or restore them.
discover.setup: To bring in backups from another installation, first set up the <storage>external storage</storage> and look for them here.
discover.none: There is no complete backup in the storage's “backups” folder.
discover.known_one: Storage has {{count}} backup, and it was already in the list.
discover.known_other: Storage has {{count}} backups, and they were already in the list.
discover.added_one: {{count}} backup was added to the list.
discover.added_other: {{count}} backups were added to the list.
discover.addedSome_one: {{count}} backup was added to the list; the others in storage were already there.
discover.addedSome_other: {{count}} backups were added to the list; the others in storage were already there.

remove.title: Delete the backup
remove.body: The backup of {{date}} is deleted. This cannot be undone.
remove.bodyRemote: The backup of {{date}} is deleted, from external storage too. This cannot be undone.

restoreDialog.title: Restore this backup
restoreDialog.lead: The platform will go back to how it was on {{date}}.
restoreDialog.lose: Everything after that backup is lost, in every account: trips, vehicles, users, alerts and settings.
restoreDialog.undo: A backup of how everything is now is saved first. With it you can undo this restore.
restoreDialog.stop: The platform stops for a few minutes. GPS devices that report in the meantime lose that data, unless the device stores and resends it.
restoreDialog.passwords: Anyone who created or changed their password after that backup signs in with the old one, and you may have to sign in again.

accounts.failed: We couldn't complete the action. Try again.
accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.searchPlaceholder: Search by account or owner's email

dialog.title: Account
dialog.suspendUserNote: Suspending a user closes their sessions and keeps them out of every account until you reactivate them; their accounts stay as they are. Deleting them erases them for good, together with the accounts they own.
dialog.deleteUserBody: The person {{email}} is erased for good and, with them, the accounts they own, with all their vehicles, devices, history and files. From other accounts they only leave. This cannot be undone.

suspension.reason: Reason: {{reason}} Its users cannot use it.
suspension.noReason: No reason noted. Its users cannot use it.
suspension.title: Suspend the account
suspension.note: Nobody can use it while it is suspended: its users see it blocked and can switch to other accounts they have. The devices keep storing data, in case it is reactivated.

limits.title: Quotas
limits.note: Leave a field empty for no limit. A quota does not delete what the account already has.

modules.title: Optional modules
modules.note: Which modules each account has is recorded; they are turned on as they are built.

delete.title: Delete the account
delete.note: Its vehicles, GPS devices, history, files and activity log are erased for good. Its users are not deleted: they only leave it, and whoever has no other account gets an empty one when they sign in again. This cannot be undone.
delete.ownerNote: It is the account of the platform's owner: it cannot be deleted.

vehicleGroups.name: Group name
vehicleGroups.note: Deleting a group does not delete its vehicles: they are left without a group.

modules.loadGroupsFailed: We couldn't load your groups. Check your connection and try again.
modules.loadVehiclesFailed: We couldn't load your vehicles. Check your connection and try again.

updates.title: Platform version
updates.upToDate: This installation has the latest version.
updates.none: No version has been published yet.
updates.off: Looking for new versions is off: the UPDATE_REPOSITORY variable is empty.

error.unreachable: GitHub could not be reached. It tries again by itself; what is shown is the last thing known.
error.rate_limited: GitHub asked to wait before checking again. It tries again by itself in a while.
error.unexpected: GitHub answered something unexpected. It tries again by itself in a while.

install.confirmBody: During the update, the platform may be out of service for a few seconds and will come back by itself.
install.requested: Backup ready. Waiting for the helper to install {{version}}…
install.running: Installing {{version}}. The platform restarts and this page reloads by itself.
install.ok: The platform was updated to version {{version}} ({{when}}).
install.manual: This installation is updated by hand: with Docker Compose, follow "Install a new version" in the guide; with Dokploy or Coolify, deploy again to install {{version}}.
install.source: This platform was built from the code: it is updated with git pull and building again.

reasons.backup: The backup before it could not be made, so {{version}} was not installed. Nothing changed.
reasons.invalid: The request to install {{version}} was not valid. Nothing changed.
reasons.unsupported: The helper cannot install versions in this installation. Nothing changed.
reasons.pull: The images of {{version}} could not be downloaded. Nothing changed: try again in a while.
reasons.files: The installation's files could not be prepared for {{version}}. Nothing changed.
reasons.env: The installation's variables do not work for {{version}}: it may need a new one (see its notes). Nothing changed.
reasons.start: The helper could not start installing {{version}}. Nothing changed.
reasons.rolled_back: Version {{version}} did not start, so it went back to {{from}} by itself.
reasons.restored: Neither {{version}} nor {{from}} started, so the backup made just before was restored.
reasons.broken: Neither {{version}} nor {{from}} started, and the backup could not be restored: the server needs checking.
reasons.cut: Installing {{version}} was cut halfway. The files of {{from}} are back: check the server.

find.label: Brand or model of your GPS
find.placeholder: Type to search: FMC920, ST-901, GT06N…
find.hint: {{models}} models in {{families}} families. If yours is not there, choose “another model” of its brand.
find.empty: We did not find that model. Type the brand and choose “another model” of it.
find.needed: Choose the brand or the model of your GPS.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.lead: Sign in without a password, with Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello, your fingerprint or a security key. Each passkey stays on your device or in your keychain (iCloud, Google) and only works on this platform.
passkeys.name: Name
passkeys.deleteBody: “{{name}}” will no longer sign you in here. Delete it from your device or keychain too.

errors.cancelled: It was cancelled or timed out. Try again.
errors.already: This device already has a passkey for your account.
errors.device: The device could not use the passkey. Try again or sign in another way.
errors.notFresh: For your security, sign in again to create a passkey, then repeat this step.
errors.unknown: That passkey is no longer on this platform. Sign in another way and delete it from your device.
errors.failed: The passkey could not be checked. Try again.
